The Cauchy–Schwarz equality condition is that all clocks coincide, since every amplitude is positive. Otherwise strict concavity up to R(T_*)=0 puts the extrapolated secant strictly above zero at T_*, and its slope is negative. In two modes, R=x(x+Delta)/((a+b)x+a Delta); taking its divided difference and its secant intercept gives the stated delay, which is b Delta divided by (a+b)+a Delta(1/x_1+1/x_2)+a Delta^2/(x_1 x_2). This gives the sign, strict monotonicity, two limits and sharp bound. In z the exponent excess is 2abz(1-z)^2/(a+bz^2)^2; its derivative has sign a(1-3z)-bz^2(3-z), strictly decreasing through zero before 1/3. For equal amplitudes the cubic has admissible root 2-sqrt(3), where substitution gives excess 1/4. With r=b/a the root equation first gives z_*=O(r^(-1/2)), then r z_*^2=1/3+O(r^(-1/2)); substitution gives the claimed square-root leading coefficient and O(1) remainder. The theorem applies to the stipulated positive, noiseless additive velocity model, not physical or operational failure prediction.
